title: Distribution and behavior of lipid droplets in hepatic cells analyzed by variations of citochemical technique and scanning electron microscopy
author: Lima-Faria, Guimarães, et al.

steps.title: Expose fish to pesticide
steps.instruction: House female Poecilia reticulata and expose them to phosphomethylglycine pesticide for 21 days.

steps.title: Sacrifice and dissect liver
steps.instruction: After exposure, sacrifice the fish, cool them, position them supine, dissect to extract the liver, and divide each liver into two fragments.

steps.title: Primary fixation of fragments
steps.instruction: Fix the liver fragments for 24 h in 2.5 % glutaraldehyde solution prepared in 0.1 M sodium phosphate buffer, keeping the samples at 4 °C.

steps.title: Post‑fixation with osmium tetroxide
steps.instruction: Post‑fix the fragments for 2 h in 1 % osmium tetroxide solution, also at 4 °C.

description: For the light microscopy evaluations Fig. 1B shows the difference of the tissue stained with Mayer's hematoxylin when compared to Fig. 1A without hematoxylin. Similarly, toluidine blue staining is validated by comparing the images with the traditional staining method (Fig. 3A and C) and those with osmium-fixed material (Fig. 3B and D). The SEM-BEC technique was validated by performing elemental analysis by energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), as shown in Fig. 6, confirming the presence of osmium in regions of intense bright staining the lipid droplets.Fig. 6Elemental analysis by energy dispersive Xray spectroscopy (EDS) in liver tissue of Poecilia reticulata. The spectrums correspond to highlighted zones in electronmicrography and it is possible to note the osmium presence (bulk arrow) in lipid droplets.Fig 6
